display.purpose: Page title and the visitor's own quoted question only.

body.purpose: The assistant's voice and all interface chrome.

components.name: Primary Button (Submit)
components.description: The send/submit control at the end of the input bar. The only button with a filled background at rest.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary" aria-label="Submit"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><polyline points="9 10 4 15 9 20"></polyline><path d="M20 4v7a4 4 0 0 1-4 4H4"></path></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; width:32px; height:32px; padding:0; border:none; border-radius:0.625rem; background:#b8823f; color:#12211d; cursor:pointer; transition:transform 0.15s, background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:#cca06a; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:none; box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(184,130,63,0.5); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform:translateY(1px); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Default button treatment for every action that isn't the primary send — nearly invisible at rest.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:4px; padding:6px 10px; border:none; border-radius:0.625rem; background:transparent; color:#8fa39a; font-family:'Work Sans', sans-serif; font-size:0.875rem; cursor:pointer; transition:color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color:#f2ede1; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline:none; box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(184,130,63,0.5); }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: The message textarea — barely distinct from the page at rest, gains a gold ring on focus.
components.css: .ds-input-group { display:flex; align-items:center; width:100%; border:1px solid #2a3a31; border-radius:0.625rem; background:transparent; padding-right:0.375rem; } .ds-input { flex:1; resize:none; border:none; background:transparent; color:#f2ede1; font-family:'Work Sans', sans-serif; font-size:1.125rem; padding:0.5rem 0.625rem; outline:none; } .ds-input::placeholder { color:#8fa39a; } .ds-input-group:focus-within { border-color:#b8823f; box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(184,130,63,0.5); }

components.name: Visitor Quote (signature component)
components.description: How a visitor's own question renders — an oversized gold serif quotation mark followed by italic serif text. The product's signature pattern.
components.html: “What's Oscar's favorite project?
components.css: .ds-quote { display:flex; gap:8px; align-items:flex-start; } .ds-quote-mark { font-family:'Fraunces', Georgia, serif; font-style:italic; font-size:1.875rem; line-height:1; color:#b8823f; user-select:none; } .ds-quote-text { font-family:'Fraunces', Georgia, serif; font-style:italic; font-size:1.25rem; color:#f2ede1; }

narrative.overview:
This is a naturalist's field notebook, not a SaaS chat widget: deep forest green stands in for a well-worn cover, warm gold leaf marks the parts worth noticing, and cream text sits on the page like ink. The whole interface is built around a single conceit — a visitor's question renders as a quoted, hand-annotated line in the margin (large italic serif, a real curly quotation mark in gold), and Oscar's answer reads back as plain typed text underneath. There is no bubble, no card, no shadow anywhere in the product; the page is genuinely flat, and the only structure comes from thin 1px gold or hairline-green rules, used the way a journal uses a ruled line rather than a box.

The palette and type pairing (serif display italics against a clean geometric sans body) both do real work: the serif quote marks the question as something personal and human-authored, while the sans-serif answer reads as considered, typed, deliberate. Nothing here should ever read as a typical AI-chat product — no rounded bubble columns, no avatar icons, no card elevation, no bright SaaS blue.
keyCharacteristics: Flat by default — zero shadows, zero card backgrounds, anywhere in the product
One accent color (gold), used sparingly and only with intent
Serif italics exclusively mark the visitor's own words; the assistant's voice is always the plain sans body
Structure comes from thin hairline rules, never boxes or borders-as-containers
Generous negative space; the page breathes like a printed page, not a dense app shell

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Gold appears in small, precise strokes only — a 1px rule, a glyph, a ring — never as a fill covering more than a button.

rules.name: The Flat Ledger Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow appears anywhere in this product. Depth and grouping come only from color contrast and hairline rules, never elevation.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Only a visitor's own words ever appear in the italic serif quote treatment. The assistant's voice is never italicized and never rendered as a quote.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift. A hairline divider is the only separator this product uses.

rules.name: The Quiet Button Rule
rules.body: Every button that isn't the primary send action stays nearly invisible until interacted with — restraint is the point, not a lesser treatment.

rules.name: The Header Rule
rules.body: The header never gains a background, border-box, or shadow of its own; it is typography and one hairline, nothing else.

dos: Do keep gold leaf rare — a rule, a ring, a glyph, one filled button.
Do render any user-authored text in italic Fraunces; keep every system/assistant voice in plain Work Sans.
Do use a 1px hairline as the only separator between regions — never a box, card, or shadow.
Do keep the reading column narrow (max-w-2xl) even as new features are added.
donts: Don't add a chat-bubble treatment, avatar icons, or card backgrounds to messages.
Don't introduce a second accent color or a bright/saturated blue.
Don't add box-shadows, drop-shadows, or any elevation effect anywhere in the product.
